title: U.S. Senate · Arkansas

context.text: This is a regularly scheduled election for the Class II Senate seat held by incumbent Tom Cotton (R), who first took office in 2015. Cotton defeated Micah Ashby and Jeb Little 81.6%-9.2%-9.1% in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary. Hallie Shoffner defeated Ethan Dunbar 78.3%-21.7% in the Democratic primary; Dan Whitfield and James Russell withdrew from that primary before the vote. Jeff Wadlin advanced as the Libertarian Party nominee from a February 22, 2026 party convention.

positions.summary: Introduced the Deportation Acceleration Act in January 2026, which would make any noncitizen convicted of a felony or two misdemeanors automatically deportable and subject them to expedited removal.
positions.quote: My bill will ensure these criminals are swiftly deported

positions.summary: In a March 18, 2026 Senate floor speech, urged senators to pass the SAVE America Act and cited public support for requiring proof of citizenship to vote.
positions.quote: I urge all senators to vote for the SAVE America Act.

positions.summary: In a March 18, 2026 Senate floor speech, urged colleagues to reject a war powers resolution on Iran, saying the strikes were within the president's constitutional authority as commander-in-chief.
positions.quote: Operation Epic Fury was well within the president’s constitutional authority and duty as commander-in-chief to defend Americans.

record.text: Currently chairs the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence and sits on the Committee on Armed Services (Subcommittees on Airland, Cybersecurity, Emerging Threats and Capabilities, and Strategic Forces), the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources, and the Joint Economic Committee.

priorities.text: Lower the cost of living for working families, including groceries, childcare, housing, and healthcare; raise the minimum wage.
Protect and strengthen Social Security and Medicare, including lifting the payroll-tax contribution cap on high earners.
Make healthcare more affordable by strengthening the Affordable Care Act, lowering prescription drug prices, and protecting Medicaid.
Support unions and workers' right to organize and bargain collectively.
Support Arkansas farmers and rural communities through regional food systems and a farm bill that expands market access.

positions.summary: Says she will fight to strengthen the Affordable Care Act, protect Medicare and Medicaid, and lower prescription drug prices.
positions.quote: I will fight to protect our hospitals, lower prescription drug prices, strengthen the Affordable Care Act, protect Medicare and Medicaid, cut red tape, and hold insurance companies accountable.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for raising the minimum wage as part of an "Arkansas-first economic plan."
positions.quote: That means raising the minimum wage, expanding workforce training, cutting taxes for working families, giving local businesses the resources they need to thrive, cutting red tape, and modernizing infrastructure.

positions.summary: Says she would lift the Social Security payroll-tax contribution cap on the "ultra wealthy" and opposes tax cuts she says benefited billionaires.
positions.quote: I will protect and strengthen Social Security and Medicare, lift the contribution cap on the ultra wealthy, reverse the cuts, and invest in a care economy that creates good-paying jobs and keeps seniors close to home.

candidates.name: Jeff Wadlin
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Libertarian Party's February 22, 2026 state convention.

priorities.text: "My first economic priority is affordability. We should eliminate broad tariffs that raise the price of food, equipment, vehicles, building materials, and household goods"
"My goal is straightforward: cover everyone, which requires cutting the total cost of healthcare roughly in half over time."
"Protect democracy. Defend personal liberty. Create broad-based prosperity."

positions.summary: His campaign issues page says he opposes broad tariffs and favors eliminating them.
positions.quote: I oppose broad tariffs that raise the cost of equipment, fertilizer, fuel, and household goods while inviting retaliation against Arkansas rice, soybeans, poultry, cotton, and other exports.

positions.summary: His campaign issues page says he supports gradual and predictable minimum-wage increases.
positions.quote: I support lower taxes on labor, gradual and predictable minimum-wage increases, stronger pathways into skilled careers

positions.summary: His campaign issues page says he would restore Congress's constitutional war powers and opposes military action Congress has not authorized.
positions.quote: I oppose wars of aggression and open-ended military action that Congress has not authorized.

positions.summary: His campaign issues page says he supports secure storage around children and rejects bans and feature-based classifications of firearms.
positions.quote: But I reject vague bans, arbitrary feature-based classifications, and laws that burden ordinary citizens while criminals ignore them.

positions.summary: His campaign issues page supports prompt removal of people who pose security risks or commit serious crimes, and says enforcement should respect due process and treat families humanely.
positions.quote: People who pose security risks or commit serious crimes should be removed promptly.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements come from the Issues page of his campaign site; no Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey responses were found. His page does not mention Israel, police funding, school choice, rent regulation, child care or transgender sports.

statements.quote: My goal is straightforward: cover everyone, which requires cutting the total cost of healthcare roughly in half over time.
I support a progressive tax system in which those with greater wealth contribute more, while working families are not disproportionately burdened by regressive taxes on wages and basic necessities.
Any new citizenship-documentation requirement must be implemented carefully, with adequate time, funding, and practical assistance for local election officials and individual voters.
statements.context: On his campaign issues page, in a passage about the SAVE Act

statements.quote: After the Supreme Court’s Dobbs decision, abortion policy is governed primarily by the states, and I do not intend to make it the centerpiece of my campaign for federal office.
Federal policy should reduce financing and infrastructure barriers while leaving zoning primarily to state and local governments, encouraging more housing construction.
Climate change is real, human activity contributes to it, and it’s affecting all of us, especially farmers.
